ROOT-CAUSED and FIXED the 6-max blueprint plateau (commit b739363). It was a TRAINER BUG, not undertraining or a coarse abstraction (both earlier hypotheses wrong). Mechanism: BlueprintTrainer + reference MCCFRTrainer dealt a FRESH hand per traverser inside each iteration; new_hand() does button=(button+1)%n, so n deals advanced the button a full cycle per iteration, phase-locking (first_to_act - traverser) to a constant. The traverser was pinned to ONE button-relative seat (empirically after=3), so every other seat's decisions -- including the UTG open where AA/KK first act (after=5) -- accumulated average strategy (huge strategy_sum mass) but EXACTLY-ZERO regret, leaving regret-matching at uniform forever. That is why AA opened identically to 72o and the BB/100 curve was flat at ~-485. Found via the diagnose_blueprint autopsy (frozen probes) + systematic-debugging instrumentation (per-(live,after) regret-vs-mass breakdown showed the after-specific zero-regret pattern, reproduced single-thread). Fix: deal ONE hand per iteration, traverse it once per seat on clones (root=new_hand(); for p: traverse(root->clone(),p)). Applied to both trainers (parity invariant). Regression test_utg_open_decisions_receive_regret asserts the UTG open accrues regret; post-fix the traverser covers all 6 seats (was 1). Both Kuhn -1/18 gates still pass, determinism preserved. CONSEQUENCE: every existing sixmax/checkpoints/*.bin was trained on the broken objective and is INVALID -- retrain from scratch, then re-run eval_sixmax_baseline.py to confirm the curve moves. FIXED the full-suite neural_cfr 'autograd engine was called while holding the GIL' crash (root cause, not symptom). Context/method (systematic-debugging): the full suite failed 1+4 only when tests/sixmax ran first; minimal repro was tests/sixmax/test_dream_kuhn.py (module-level `import torch`) + any neural_cfr backward.
